Antigravity executor contract (packages/gateway-daemon/src/agy-planner-executor.ts): opt-in on Linux via BUILDROOM_PLANNER_EXECUTOR set to agy, pinned to Gateway 1880c12d-d98d-4a91-b25a-23320aa7f58a and the ratified architect seat (google / gemini-4-argon, effort high, agy model gemini-4-argon-high), verifying binary SHA-256 (BUILDROOM_PLANNER_AGY_SHA256), running sudo -n -u <plannerUser> against a read-only checkout at baseSha with --mode plan --sandbox, holding back the prompt until the stream-json init event confirms model gemini-4-argon-high and records conversation_id, and halting via planner-halted.json on any process/cleanup/evidence anomaly.
data_flow: The README.md section will trace the end-to-end data flow of a Phase 4 planner round and decision: 1. Scope Capture (T1): A room transitions to SCOPED via scope.captured; prepareFounderGoal validates the Founder's goal (non-empty, at most 20,000 characters, free of credential material) and binds the server-derived founder_goal SHA-256 digest into the T1 event payload and evidence. 2. Opening the Round (T2 or T4 retry): Under the fenced room lock (L3) and journal append lock (L4), PlannerLoop.runPlannerRound transitions SCOPED to PLANNING (T2 task.dispatched.planner with server-derived G2 guard facts rolesAssigned, reviewerIsNotBuilder across distinct surfaces, and fence-derived gatewayOnline) and appends the command's journaled row in the same database transaction. When already in PLANNING (after a T4 plan.revision_requested or a not_sent retry within the 3-attempt round budget), it journals the next deterministic command attempt under the room lock bound to the opening T2 or T4 event. 3. Route Authorization, Attestation, and Identity Binding: Before any dispatch, the loop checks authorizeRoute against the ratified seat registry and requests planner.attest(commandId) over GatewayPlannerChannel. On valid attestation matching the intended provider, model, and execution surface, the loop journals identity_bound. 4. Dispatch and Execution: The loop calls planner.dispatch(work). GatewayPlannerChannel delivers the execute request on poll (or withdraws it as not_sent if never polled before timeout). GatewayPlannerWorker persists a durable record under planner/<sha256(commandId)>.json (attested -> starting -> running -> finished, or not_sent / lost). In agy mode, AgyPlannerExecutor verifies no lingering planner-user processes, checks the agy binary SHA-256, creates a read-only git checkout at baseSha, spawns agy --mode plan --sandbox, verifies init.model === 'gemini-4-argon-high' and captures conversation_id before writing the prompt to stdin, persists supplemental evidence, and returns the raw stdout. The control plane verifies the observed route and required init fields and journals dispatched (BRJ:c:2 with init_model and provider_conversation_id). 5. Plan Judgment and Submission (T3): planner.awaitPlan(commandId) returns the raw output. judgeRoundPlan validates PLANDOC_SCHEMA_V1, terminal_status === 'PLAN_READY_FOR_FOUNDER_APPROVAL', and that repository, base_sha, and scope_paths lie within captured T1 scope. On success, submitRoundPlan commits T3 plan.submitted (moving the room to PLAN_REVIEW), PlanStore.recordPlan (computing BRJ:b:1 plan_hash), and the journal's completed row (verified by the section 5.3 CompletionAuthorizationResolver) in one transaction. 6. Founder Review and Decision (T4, T5, T22): The Founder reads the submitted plan via GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan and submits a decision via POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision. In a single transaction under the room lock, the route re-reads and re-verifies the stored plan, derives G4/G5/G22 guard facts on the server, appends the lifecycle event (T4 back to PLANNING for another round, T5 to PLAN_APPROVED, or T22 to CANCELLED after marking any pending planner commands unresolved), and appends the journal decision row.
trust_and_security_boundaries: The documentation will highlight the built trust and security boundaries: 1. Token separation: CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN (room events and plan read), PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN (solely for POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision), and PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN_TOKEN (solely for the counted-run router; rejected if equal to CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN or PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN). 2. Governed path enforcement: Direct injection of T2, T3, T4, T5, or T22 via POST /rooms/:roomId/events is rejected with HTTP 403 governed_path_required. 3. Sole-writer database latch and lock ordering: Only JournalStore calls command_journal_append, setting app.journal_writer = 'br_app_runtime' inside the transaction and acquiring L4 advisory lock 8_201_015 after L3 room lock. 4. Credential-material screening: Journal payloads, founder goals, revision feedback, and every key and string of stored PlanDocs are screened by containsCredentialMaterial before persistence; refusal reasons on planner.plan_refused log lines are restricted to a closed enum so raw planner output cannot leak into logs. 5. Outbound-only Gateway pull and OS-isolated executor: The Gateway polls the control plane using Ed25519-signed envelopes; AgyPlannerExecutor runs on Linux under a dedicated OS user via sudo -n -u against a read-only checkout with --mode plan --sandbox, verifies binary SHA-256, withholds the prompt until model init confirmation, kills residual user processes on exit, and latches planner-halted.json on any cleanup or evidence fault.

error_and_failure_behavior: The README.md section will document how the built planner loop handles failures and recovery: 1. Pre-send refusals (route authorization failure, attestation failure, or identity mismatch) append failed with pre_send_refusal and leave the room in PLANNING without contacting the provider. 2. Confirmed unsent dispatches (Gateway never polled before timeout or executor verified not_sent before prompt write) append failed with not_sent and are eligible for Q8 retry within the 3-attempt round budget. 3. Ambiguous transport or mid-execution failures (dispatch throw after delivery, missing init_model/conversation_id on an initRequired lane, awaitPlan timeout/throw, or Gateway restart turning starting/running into lost) append unresolved and halt automatic retry until reconciled. 4. Post-execution refusals (route_mismatch, planner_reported_failure, plan_invalid, or plan_outside_captured_scope) append failed with a closed-set reason and log planner.plan_refused without raw output. 5. Crash recovery (PlannerRecovery): verifies the journal chain from genesis first, then queries PlannerPort.reconcile by commandId without re-dispatching; only an explicit reconciled determination resolves an unresolved command, whereas ambiguous or mismatch leaves it unresolved. 6. Counted-run E2 live check: on Phase4-CR1 round 1, if the first dispatched row lacks init_model or provider_conversation_id, the harness fails the run before Founder review and issues a single founder.cancel cleanup request.
observability: The README.md section will document the built observability surfaces: 1. Hash-chained command journal (public.command_journal) with BRJ:c:2 command rows, BRJ:d:1 decision rows, BRJ:b:1 plan hashes, and full chain verification/reconstruction via GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal during counted runs. 2. Sanitized structured log event planner.plan_refused carrying only roomId, commandId, and closed-set reason (not_json, schema_invalid, terminal_status_not_ready, scope_mismatch, or credential_material). 3. Gateway durable per-command records (planner/<sha256(commandId)>.json), AgyPlannerExecutor supplemental evidence files (planner-executor-evidence/<sha256(commandId)>.json), and the halt latch file (planner-halted.json). 4. Phase 4 counted-run artifacts written by packages/run-harness/src/phase4/cli.ts under the run directory (attempts.json, run.lock, per-run JSON records, and <label>-plan.json saved at PLAN_REVIEW).
